**Yes. CAPA-26-012 and CAPA-26-015 trace back to the same upstream cause: the INC-03 incubator door closure/door-alarm defect.** Their recorded root causes differ, but the evidence points to one equipment problem.

**The two CAPAs**
- **CAPA-26-012** (corrective: replace the INC-03 door switch and re-execute TC-OQ-INC-04) was raised from DEV-26-011. That deviation's recorded root cause is "door switch misaligned." The INC-03 door alarm activated at 142 s against a limit of 60 s. The CAPA is still OPEN and was due 31 Mar 2026.
- **CAPA-26-015** (corrective: retrain Suite 2 operators on the door latch check, SOP-MFG-105) was raised from DEV-26-033. That deviation's recorded root cause is "operator did not confirm door latch." On 11 Jun, INC-03's door was found not fully latched, and the alarm was acknowledged at 07:50. PPQ26-02 harvest viability was 75.2%, below the 80% criterion.

**Why they share a cause**
- Trace links connect both deviations to INC-03 (DEV-26-011 and DEV-26-033 both link to equipment INC-03).
- The equipment event log shows the same door-alarm failure mode on INC-03 both times. On 10 Jun 21:40 a door alarm fired and was not acknowledged until 07:50 the next morning. A temperature-low alarm on the same unit started at 22:22.
- The fix for the first failure was never implemented. Change control CC-26-019 (INC-03 door switch replacement and re-execution of TC-OQ-INC-04) is linked to CAPA-26-012 and is still "APPROVED – NOT IMPLEMENTED." The door-switch defect was therefore still present when PPQ26-02 ran.
- CAPA-26-015 addresses the operator step only. Its effectiveness check is still PENDING, and it was closed without the equipment fix.

So the operator error in DEV-26-033 was likely a symptom of an unresolved door-latch/alarm defect on INC-03. Retraining alone will not close it. The overdue CC-26-019 implementation and the CAPA-26-012 closure should be addressed first.

**Not a shared cause (checked)**
- CAPA-26-008 (FRZ-80-02 compressor) is linked only to DEV-26-021. It does not link to any other CAPA.
- CAPA-26-016 (DEV-26-027, low CAR+ in ENG26-01/02) is recorded as donor CD3 variability. The data does not support that. Donor CD3% in the PPQ runs (50–66%) is similar to the ENG runs, yet CAR+ was 37–45% in PPQ runs. All three ENG runs used vector lot LV25-118 and had CAR+ of 12–20%. The material record places LV25-118 in FRZ-80-02, the freezer from DEV-26-021. However, DEV-26-021 says contents were relocated to FRZ-80-01, so the link is unconfirmed. This is a lead for investigation, not an established shared cause, and it is not trace-linked in the database.
- CAPA-26-019 (supplier sampling-port weld defect) is a separate supplier issue.

**Yes. CAPA-26-012 and CAPA-26-015 trace back to the same upstream cause: the INC-03 incubator door closure/door-alarm defect.** Their recorded root causes differ, but the evidence points to one equipment problem.

**The two CAPAs**
- **CAPA-26-012** (corrective: replace the INC-03 door switch and re-execute TC-OQ-INC-04) was raised from DEV-26-011. That deviation's recorded root cause is "door switch misaligned." The INC-03 door alarm activated at 142 s against a limit of 60 s. The CAPA is still OPEN and was due 31 Mar 2026.
- **CAPA-26-015** (corrective: retrain Suite 2 operators on the door latch check, SOP-MFG-105) was raised from DEV-26-033. That deviation's recorded root cause is "operator did not confirm door latch." On 11 Jun, INC-03's door was found not fully latched, and the alarm was acknowledged at 07:50. PPQ26-02 harvest viability was 75.2%, below the 80% criterion.

**Why they share a cause**
- Trace links connect both deviations to INC-03 (DEV-26-011 and DEV-26-033 both link to equipment INC-03).
- The equipment event log shows the same door-alarm failure mode on INC-03 both times. On 10 Jun 21:40 a door alarm fired and was not acknowledged until 07:50 the next morning. A temperature-low alarm on the same unit started at 22:22.
- The fix for the first failure was never implemented. Change control CC-26-019 (INC-03 door switch replacement and re-execution of TC-OQ-INC-04) is linked to CAPA-26-012 and is still "APPROVED – NOT IMPLEMENTED." The door-switch defect was therefore still present when PPQ26-02 ran.
- CAPA-26-015 addresses the operator step only. Its effectiveness check is still PENDING, and it was closed without the equipment fix.

So the operator error in DEV-26-033 was likely a symptom of an unresolved door-latch/alarm defect on INC-03. Retraining alone will not close it. The overdue CC-26-019 implementation and the CAPA-26-012 closure should be addressed first.

**Not a shared cause (checked)**
- CAPA-26-008 (FRZ-80-02 compressor) is linked only to DEV-26-021. It does not link to any other CAPA.
- CAPA-26-016 (DEV-26-027, low CAR+ in ENG26-01/02) is recorded as donor CD3 variability. The data does not support that. Donor CD3% in the PPQ runs (50–66%) is similar to the ENG runs, yet CAR+ was 37–45% in PPQ runs. All three ENG runs used vector lot LV25-118 and had CAR+ of 12–20%. The material record places LV25-118 in FRZ-80-02, the freezer from DEV-26-021. However, DEV-26-021 says contents were relocated to FRZ-80-01, so the link is unconfirmed. This is a lead for investigation, not an established shared cause, and it is not trace-linked in the database.
- CAPA-26-019 (supplier sampling-port weld defect) is a separate supplier issue.
